 50,000 Americans getting automatic $5,000 refunds from IRS: Here’s who qualifies
 The IRS has begun automatic adoption credit refunds affecting more than 50,000 taxpayers. Eligible unused credits can increase the refundable amount for 2025, subject to a $5,000 per-child limit. Most adjustments require no action, although missing return information may need correction. 
 Michael Brown 
 - Contributor
 Oct 23, 2026 
 Comments 
 The Internal Revenue Service has begun issuing automatic refunds to more than 50,000 taxpayers following a change in how unused adoption tax credits are treated. The agency announced the refunds on October 16, 2026, with most eligible taxpayers expected to have their cases completed by year-end.
 The adjustment allows qualifying adoption credit carryforwards from 2020 through 2024 to increase the refundable adoption credit for tax year 2025. The refundable portion is capped at $5,000 per eligible child.
 IRS COVID Tax Refund July 2026: Who May Qualify and Why July 10 Matters However, the amount each taxpayer receives depends on their credit entitlement and tax account. Some may receive a smaller refund or a reduction in outstanding taxes.
 Table of Contents
 Who Qualifies for the IRS Adoption Credit Adjustment? 
 Will Every Eligible Taxpayer Receive $5,000? 
 When Will the Automatic Refunds Arrive? 
 Do Taxpayers Need to File an Amended Return? 
 How to Check the Adjustment 
 What This Means for the Next Tax Return 
 Who Qualifies for the IRS Adoption Credit Adjustment? 
 The IRS is reviewing 2025 tax accounts where available records show an unused adoption credit that could increase the refundable amount.
 Potentially eligible taxpayers include those who:
 Filed a 2025 federal individual income tax return.
 Claimed, or were eligible to claim, the adoption credit.
 Had qualifying unused adoption credits available for use in 2025.
 Have return and account information supporting an increased refundable credit.
 An adoption credit carryforward is an unused credit carried into a later tax year. These credits generally have a five-year carryforward period, making credits originating from 2020 through 2024 potentially relevant to this adjustment.
 Will Every Eligible Taxpayer Receive $5,000? 
 No. The $5,000 figure is the maximum refundable adoption credit per eligible child for 2025.
 The actual result depends on the available credit, applicable limits and the taxpayer’s account. Outstanding debts may also reduce the payment.
 Taxpayers who already received the correct refundable credit may have no additional adjustment.
 When Will the Automatic Refunds Arrive? 
 Refunds and account adjustments began in late September 2026 . The IRS expects to complete the process for most eligible taxpayers by the end of the year.
 Eligible taxpayers who filed their 2025 returns before April 15, 2026, will generally receive the adjustment automatically.
 Extension filers and taxpayers with identity theft indicators, account freezes, dependency conflicts or other unresolved issues will be reviewed later in 2026 after processing or resolution. The announcement does not provide one payment date for every recipient.
 Do Taxpayers Need to File an Amended Return? 
 Most affected taxpayers should not file an amended return solely to request the automatic adjustment.
 An exception may arise when the IRS lacks sufficient information—for example, if a return omitted the adoption credit carryforward. A taxpayer may then need Form 1040-X, with the relevant adoption credit information, to correct the return.
 Other errors on a 2025 return may also require a separate amendment.
 How to Check the Adjustment 
 The IRS generally sends a notice within 30 days of adjusting an account. It explains the change and whether the amount produced a refund or was applied to another tax or non-tax debt.
 Taxpayers should compare the notice with their 2025 return and retain it.
 Where’s My Refund? will not display this type of adjustment. Taxpayers should instead review their notice, IRS Individual Online Account or tax account transcript.
 What This Means for the Next Tax Return 
 The special treatment of prior-year carryforwards applies to tax year 2025 only. Receiving an adjustment does not make those carryforwards refundable again in 2026.
 Affected taxpayers should retain their corrected credit records because the adjustment may reduce the unused credit available for future years.
